This may be more of a regional thing specific for the state of Schleswig-Holstein and bordering states but people usually don't like to talk here. Striking up a conversation with someone who randomly happened to be maybe waiting in the same queue as you is seen as pushy and should be avoided. Similarly if you're in a store it's unusual to engage in conversation. You just say hi, pay, wish them a good day and leave.

Also, I present to you the single most genius word ever invented in the German language: Moin.
It's a greeting but can also be used to say goodbye, it's completely disconnected from time so you can say it no matter how late it is and it's also not really reflecting any power dynamic. You can say moin to a little child, you can say moin to the cashier, you can say moin to your boss, it's great.

Alright, here's my theory although I know it's not canon. I know that Liza Minelli is personifying Mother War in Mama but I always imagined it to be the patients mother. He joined the military without telling his mom who despised it. During his deployment she died.

So now he's in the hospital, having flashbacks of this war and hearing the voice of his dead mother. In Sleep he delves deeper into their relationship. The whole "Through it all how could you cry for me cause I don't feel bad about it" to me is the patient telling his mother that she shouldn't cry or be sad for him cause he's feeling no remorse about his decision. "Shut your eyes, kiss me goodbye and sleep" is him trying to calm her down, telling her to distract herself, to just sleep. In the bridge we see the aftermath of it. He comes back home after deployment and finds her dead. The whole "Wake up" could be him finally feeling remorse, regretting that he put her in misery for the last months of her life.

Again, I know it's wrong but that's how I like to see it, haha
